rule: New upstream capability and new-to-this-Harness integration are separate claims. Deferred candidates have acceptance gates, not assumed gains.

candidates.novelty: Mature SQLite behavior; newly integrated failure handling in Harness 0.13.0.
candidates.gap: Corrupt indexes break known-source reads; two-character Chinese has no trigram hit; missing roots prune index entries.
candidates.experiment: Four isolated failure fixtures, then five installed CLI flows and a live known-source read.
candidates.acceptance: All fixtures recover or preserve data; no canonical writes; corrupt database unchanged; output bounded.
candidates.net_benefit: Four demonstrated failure cases corrected; direct reads bypass indexing; zero external service cost.
candidates.cost: Fallback scans at most 64 candidate files and 4 MiB; results disclose truncation. 20 tiny-fixture runs have median 1.315 ms, not a production SLA.
candidates.risk: Literal fallback can miss synonyms or content beyond the scan budget.
candidates.rollback: Restore backed-up memory_router.py and memory_search.py; Markdown remains untouched.

candidates.novelty: Apply published trace/evaluation principles to local retrieval and control-plane failures.
candidates.gap: Happy-path tests and stale PASS receipts do not prove degraded behavior.
candidates.experiment: Database corruption, lock contention, missing root, invalid UTF-8, path escape, and protected-file hashes.
candidates.acceptance: Deterministic regression suite plus installed CLI tests; distinguish static automation checks from scheduler outcomes.
candidates.net_benefit: Failure handling is reproducible, with explicit scope and private-data preservation evidence.
candidates.cost: Local tests only; no paid model evaluation or telemetry upload.
candidates.risk: Does not measure live model routing quality or full agent success rate.
candidates.rollback: Revert versioned tests and audit additions.

candidates.novelty: New local measurement integration; current official runtime is independently observed.
candidates.gap: Prompt probe selects old PATH CLI while config gate selects Desktop CLI; old audit tokens lack date and scope.
candidates.experiment: Default probe fails before fix; same resolved CLI succeeds before/after with identical working directory.
candidates.acceptance: Default invocation succeeds; record CLI identity, time and measurement scope; no config edits.
candidates.net_benefit: Removes false measurement failures and prevents presenting CLI estimates as live Desktop usage.
candidates.cost: Small local version-resolution probes; no inference request.
candidates.risk: CLI catalog differs from the active Desktop conversation.
candidates.rollback: Restore backed-up measurement and audit scripts.

candidates.novelty: Existing routing pattern applied to the owned introspection skill.
candidates.gap: Entry mixes repeated scope lists with upgrade-only detail.
candidates.experiment: Keep description stable; move upgrade acceptance into a conditional reference; rerun 50 trigger contracts.
candidates.acceptance: Entry 802 to 454 o200k tokens; all trigger contracts pass; full upgrade branch remains linked.
candidates.net_benefit: 348 fewer tokens when entry is loaded for ordinary introspection; startup unchanged.
candidates.cost: Upgrade tasks load a separate reference and may read more total text.
candidates.risk: Deterministic trigger contracts are not a live model benchmark.
candidates.rollback: Restore skill directory from baseline tag.

candidates.novelty: Code execution and selective tool discovery reduce model-visible catalogs.
candidates.gap: Large tool/document responses consume context before relevant records are selected.
candidates.experiment: Synthetic 100-tool catalog projected to five candidates: 14302 to 132 tokens.
candidates.acceptance: Future real task replay must preserve tool-selection accuracy; load full schemas before execution.
candidates.net_benefit: Payload reduction demonstrated only; no production token, latency or success gain claimed.
candidates.cost: Native code-mode capability reused; no extra server installed.
candidates.risk: Truncation can hide semantics; arbitrary code adapters expand attack surface.
candidates.rollback: Use full native tool discovery; no runtime mutation to undo.

candidates.novelty: Tasks become an extension with negotiated capabilities and polling/update APIs.
candidates.gap: No verified client/server extension negotiation for the local adapters.
candidates.experiment: Protocol review against currently configured stdio and HTTP MCP surfaces; no third-party execution.
candidates.acceptance: Both peers advertise extension support; cancellation, status scope and auth regression pass.
candidates.net_benefit: Unproven for this machine's current workflows.
candidates.cost: Adapter migration and long-running task lifecycle coverage.
candidates.rollback: Retain existing protocol adapters and pinned versions.

candidates.novelty: Current API exposes server-side compaction and cache-miss diagnostics.
candidates.gap: Harness does not own Desktop request assembly; native context management is already configured.
candidates.experiment: Read current feature keys and first-party API contracts without sending paid requests.
candidates.acceptance: An owned API workload and repeated cached_tokens/cost measurements must justify a new adapter.
candidates.net_benefit: No measured gain from a second compaction layer.
candidates.cost: API calls plus state/provenance complexity if adopted.
candidates.risk: Double compaction, losing canonical response items, unsupported Desktop config changes.
candidates.rollback: Leave current native context management unchanged.

candidates.novelty: Pins MCP 2.1.1 and release tools; retains permission/accessibility fixes.
candidates.gap: Local 0.1.8 fork contains uncommitted patches and Edge-specific compatibility.
candidates.experiment: Compare provenance and release notes; built-in Edge inventory/session-name requests fail at transport.
candidates.acceptance: Preserve and port local diff; audited dependencies; real Edge load, action, screenshot and cleanup pass.
candidates.net_benefit: Potential reliability benefit, not yet proven for the patched Edge route.
candidates.cost: Patch review and browser regression; no estimated token reduction.
candidates.risk: Overwriting active local fixes or losing a working fallback.
candidates.rollback: Preserve fork commit aa2ecb4 and existing dirty working tree; no browser files changed.

candidates.novelty: Current stable release includes update/recovery and agent runtime changes.
candidates.gap: Installed 2026.6.5 predates several migrations; authenticated channels have no isolated acceptance fixture here.
candidates.experiment: Official release/ref verification and non-secret installed package/config inventory.
candidates.acceptance: Isolated config migration and representative channel/session restore must pass before global package update.
candidates.net_benefit: Possible stability gains; current operational regression risk exceeds demonstrated benefit.
candidates.risk: Channel state or local overlays may be incompatible.
candidates.rollback: Keep installed package version and local state; no migration executed.

candidates.novelty: Curated offline Pi profile and improved incomplete-memory-read classification.
candidates.gap: Only three locally patched ECC skills are active; no Pi runtime deployment is needed.
candidates.experiment: Review release packaging boundaries and local active-slice provenance.
candidates.acceptance: Any imported file needs an exact diff, license verification and Codex trigger compatibility.
candidates.net_benefit: Adopt the failure-classification idea locally; bulk package replacement has no measured benefit.
candidates.cost: 123-skill Pi bundle would enlarge maintenance and discovery surface.
candidates.risk: Overwrite local frontmatter patches or activate foreign hooks.
candidates.rollback: Retain 37d3198 local active slice and patches.

candidates.novelty: New CLI installers, root launchers and cross-platform execution.
candidates.gap: BraveCow already owns cross-runtime installation; local upstream checkout is dirty.
candidates.experiment: Read official commit diff and compare responsibilities; distinguish similarly named research from this repository.
candidates.acceptance: Demonstrate a missing workflow without competing configuration ownership.
candidates.net_benefit: No clear gain from a second installer or automatic harness optimizer.
candidates.risk: Overlapping instruction/config writers; paper results do not transfer automatically.
candidates.rollback: Keep existing eafb747 source and local patches.

candidates.novelty: Installed plugin 0.40.0 is newer than repository's reproducible 0.39.0 pin.
candidates.gap: GitHub latest-release endpoint has no release record; native-app acceptance was not available in this session.
candidates.experiment: Validate manifest resolution: exact enabled id resolves installed 0.40.0.
candidates.acceptance: Audit a 0.40.0 source commit, build dependencies and actual UI flow before changing fresh-install pin.
candidates.net_benefit: Current machine already runs 0.40.0; no immediate upgrade gain.
candidates.cost: Build and native UI acceptance required for reproducibility.
candidates.risk: Pinning an unverified commit could break new installs.
candidates.rollback: Keep current installed plugin and source lock separately documented.

candidates.novelty: Explicit backup, encoding/secret gate and successful-write watermark contract.
candidates.gap: Existing private prompt lacks explicit backup-before-write and failure-watermark rules; stale ownership alias.
candidates.experiment: Back up definition, attempt official automation update, and compare full readback.
candidates.acceptance: API update succeeds with schedule/model/project/notification preserved; exact readback matches.
candidates.net_benefit: Pending: tool returned failure; definition is unchanged.
candidates.cost: No runtime change or extra scheduled work.
candidates.risk: Old project id is absent from current project registry; remapping it would change an explicitly preserved field.
candidates.rollback: Original definition backed up; proposed private prompt saved locally, never committed.

candidates.novelty: Optional semantic or relationship retrieval remains available as an architectural direction.
candidates.gap: No observed semantic-recall requirement justifies a persistent graph/vector service after retirement.
candidates.experiment: Local FTS5, direct Markdown and bounded degradation satisfy the exercised retrieval flows.
candidates.acceptance: Reconsider only with a representative failed-recall set and measurable gains exceeding operating cost.
candidates.net_benefit: No net gain established; preserve the retired service state.
candidates.cost: Would add daemon, dependency, synchronization, privacy and recovery costs.
candidates.risk: Duplicate truth sources and failed sync or data deletion.
candidates.rollback: No service introduced; Markdown and FTS5 remain the active path.
